statusText: The CME weekend halt still governs this assessment: nothing has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about eight hours past the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail therefore holds at 10% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than observed extension. What this hour adds is that both open threads moved away from resolution rather than toward it. On Lebanon, Israel's Prime Minister's office responded to Hezbollah's retaliation warning not with de-escalation but with an accusation that Hezbollah uses its own civilians as human shields; President Joseph Aoun said plainly that the strike carried "a clear message regarding the negotiating process and the US efforts aimed at implementing this agreement"; and the last round of US-brokered talks in Rome is confirmed to have closed on 6 August with no agreement on the timing of Israeli withdrawal. On Iran, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's stated price for reopening the strait is now sanctions relief plus war reparations, a condition set that moves the Iran-Oman track further from a near-term deal even as the IEA warns of the widest 2026 supply shortfall in five years. Stress therefore rises one point to 56% (elevated). The counterweight is unchanged and equally observed - VIX closed Friday at 14.25, less than a point above its 52-week low of 13.38, and the Nasdaq-100 closed down only 0.13% and about 2.3% below its 52-week high. Confidence is 61% (solid): NQ futures, VIX, the 10-year yield, both crude benchmarks and two independent Lebanon primaries were re-read directly this hour, while the 2-year yield and the seven-day calendar are carried forward from last hour's direct reads because dated events and a Friday close cannot change over a weekend.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk remains genuinely two-way. Pulling one way: a Lebanon escalation in which Hezbollah has promised a response and Israel has answered with a human-shields accusation rather than restraint, a negotiating track that Beirut's president now says was itself the target of the message and whose last Rome round closed on 6 August without agreement, an Iranian condition set for reopening Hormuz that has hardened to sanctions relief plus war reparations, a U.S. economic-isolation package explicitly promised for next week, 15 ADNOC vessels struck in the strait since February with the latest hit on Saturday, WTI at $82.40 after a +5% week and +33% year with an IEA deficit warning attached, and a 10Y at 4.696% pressing a 19-month high. Pulling the other: VIX within a point of its 52-week low, an index that closed the week only 0.13% lower after a third consecutive higher week, and a Friday tape that absorbed the escalation with a mid-range settle rather than a liquidation. Treat the reopen as a checkpoint to be scored on observed price path, not as a pre-committed direction. The dated calendar checkpoints begin Monday and culminate in the FOMC minutes on Wednesday; the undated one - the Treasury's Iran package - is deliberately absent from the verified calendar because no exact date has been published.
headline: Israel answers Hezbollah's retaliation warning with a human-shields accusation, Aoun says the strike targeted the negotiating track, and Iran's price for reopening Hormuz hardens to sanctions relief plus reparations - Stress 56%, Tail holds at 10% with CME shut, action EA_ON.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from the primary quote page, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, on 397,964 contracts, opening at 30,210.75 and settling inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide with no close pinned to either extreme. NQ sits about 2.7% below its 52-week high of 30,975.50 against a 52-week low of 22,961.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below its 52-week high, completing a third consecutive higher week. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency here is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than eighteen hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close, re-verified this hour where it could move). The split in the evidence remains the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60% on the day, inside a 14.18-14.72 range and only 0.87 points above its 52-week low of 13.38 against a 52-week high of 35.30. Rates and energy say the opposite. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.696%, +5.5bp on the day and at the top of a 4.625-4.700% range, pressing the 52-week high of 4.747% set earlier in the week; the 2-year closed at 4.171%, +3.1bp. The curve is therefore steepening on long-end inflation aversion rather than signalling a growth scare. WTI stands at $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day, +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and +32.95% on the year; Brent at $88.52, +$1.45 or +1.67%, +4.20% on the month and +34.43% on the year. Trading Economics attributes the move to Treasury Secretary Bessent's promised "unprecedented economic measures" against Iran, the continuing naval blockade of Iranian ports, Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure and an IEA warning of the widest 2026 global supply shortfall in five years, partly offset by additional Middle Eastern crude reaching U.S. markets. An index within 2.3% of its high while oil is up a third on the year and the long end presses a 19-month high is a conflicted configuration, and by the risk definition a conflict of that kind belongs in Stress, not in Tail.

GEOPOLITICS (new this hour). Two threads moved away from resolution rather than toward it. On Lebanon, the sequence went from Hezbollah's retaliation warning to an Israeli response that hardened rather than defused it: the Prime Minister's office said Hezbollah "is willing to do anything, including using its own civilians as human shields", answering the accusation of civilian deaths instead of the threat of retaliation. Hezbollah's own wording, confirmed against a second primary source, is that the assaults "will be met with what they deserve" and that they "cannot continue", alongside a demand that Beirut abandon the "humiliating" direct negotiations and stop relying on U.S. mediation. The casualty picture is confirmed at 11 killed - 7 in Ansar including 3 children, 4 in Deir ez-Zahrani - with 19 wounded. Most consequentially for the political track, President Joseph Aoun said the strike conveyed "a clear message regarding the negotiating process and the US efforts aimed at implementing this agreement", and it is now confirmed that the last Rome round closed on 6 August without agreement, deadlocked on the timing of Israeli withdrawal from the south. The negotiating channel Hezbollah wants abandoned was therefore already stalled before these strikes; Prime Minister Nawaf Salam separately rejected the military-target justification and reasserted that authority over any military infrastructure "lies exclusively with the Lebanese state". On Iran, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's stated conditions for reopening the strait - easing sanctions on Tehran and paying war reparations - are materially harder than the "close to an agreement" framing that had supported reopening optimism, and they sit directly against Bessent's promise of "economic isolation like the world has never seen before" plus a continued blockade. The two positions are not currently reconcilable. ADNOC's cumulative tally stands at 15 vessels struck since February, the latest on Saturday, and the wider crisis count is at least 17 merchant ships damaged with 12 seafarers killed or missing.

SCORING. Tail stays at 10%. Every ingredient the definition demands - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, price holding near extremes - requires a live tape, and there is none; the last observed tape showed the opposite. The 10% is not a claim about structure but a price for weekend headline discontinuity expressing as a Sunday gap. Stress rises one point to 56% (elevated), reflecting an Israeli response that met a retaliation warning with escalatory rhetoric, a negotiating track confirmed stalled since 6 August and now publicly identified by Lebanon's president as the target of the strike, and an Iranian condition set for Hormuz that has hardened against a U.S. position promising maximum isolation - against the genuine counterweight of a VIX near its 52-week low and an index that closed the week almost unchanged. Confidence is 61% (solid): this hour re-read NQ futures, VIX, the 10-year yield, both crude benchmarks and two independent Lebanon primaries directly, and cross-checked Hezbollah's wording across two of them; the 2-year yield and the verified seven-day calendar are carried forward from last hour's direct reads, which is legitimate because a Friday close and a set of dated releases cannot change over a weekend. One live-blog fetch was refused and was replaced by other primary sources rather than left as a gap. The remaining defect is the unavoidable staleness of the price evidence. Dominant mode is mixed: complacent equity volatility against stressed rates and energy is precisely a mixed regime, not a trend.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 7-9% across Friday's U.S. cash session, where the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress traced a clear event arc: 44% down to 40% across Friday afternoon and the U.S. cash session, then easing to 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 9-12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. From 06:00 UTC the weekend escalation sequence lifted the series steadily - Tail to 10% and Stress through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 54% and 55% - as the Mokha barrage, the Lebanon strikes, the ADNOC vessel attack, the U.S. territorial claim, Hezbollah's explicit retaliation warning and then the state-level condemnations from Salam and Aoun landed one after another with no tape to absorb them. Confidence ran 37-62%, weakest in the hours immediately around the weekly close and improving steadily from 57% to 62% across the weekend halt as each dimension was re-verified hour by hour. The 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August is unavailable because no successful Claude snapshot was published for that hour; those fields are null and no past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 15:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 14:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly eight hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% through the remaining Saturday afternoon and evening slots, ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC as the reopen edges into view and to 12% across the Sunday slots; those increments reflect accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 56% through the thin Saturday hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, firm to 57% from 20:00 UTC and to 58% from Sunday morning as the unresolved threads converge on the reopen. Confidence drifts from 61% to 55% across the horizon as the last live prints age further without replacement. The material catalyst sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which the danger window brackets. Inside the horizon the realistic risks are headline-driven - an actual Hezbollah retaliation following the warning Israel has now answered with a human-shields accusation, a formal collapse of the US-brokered track that has been stalled since the 6 August Rome round, a further Hormuz vessel strike after the sixteenth, an early leak of the Treasury's Iran package, or movement on Araghchi's hardened reopening conditions - each of which would move Stress and the expected gap rather than produce observable one-way structure. The first scheduled checkpoint is Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC; the week's highest-impact dated items are Tuesday's housing and industrial production data, the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August, Thursday's claims and Philadelphia Fed pair, and Friday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Its highest-impact undated item is the Treasury's Iran package, omitted from the calendar because no exact date has been published. Nvidia's results on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium later that month both fall outside this seven-day window.
